stories.title: New structures come into view in brain wiring maps
stories.summary: Researchers at Harvard Medical School and the University of California San Diego have accelerated imaging techniques to map large volumes of brain tissue in nanoscale detail. The approach reveals fine structures that traditional connectomes can miss. The brain is finally being asked to show its work.

stories.title: Nasal mRNA treatment improves memory in aged mice
stories.summary: Weekly nasal drops carrying mRNA for the protein BDNF matched the memory scores of 18-month-old mice to 3-month-old animals. The treatment, which also showed efficacy in mice with Alzheimer-type damage, successfully delivered protein to the hippocampus without spreading to other organs. Mice are currently enjoying the results.

stories.title: Real-world study confirms dupilumab reduces chronic prurigo nodularis itch
stories.summary: A retrospective study in Dermatology and Therapy shows that dupilumab provides durable clinical improvement for adults with chronic prurigo nodularis. By inhibiting type 2 neuro-immune signaling, the drug cleared severe skin lesions. The findings confirm efficacy previously established in randomized clinical trials, now occurring in routine practice.

stories.title: Alcohol consumption may interfere with cancer immunotherapy
stories.summary: Cancer immunotherapy has transformed treatment for advanced cancers, yet its effectiveness may depend on patient habits. A study in Science Signaling explores whether regular alcohol consumption acts as an overlooked factor in treatment outcomes. The glass of wine is being asked to justify its presence.

stories.title: Daraxonrasib combo shows promise in pancreatic cancer trial
stories.summary: A phase 1/2 trial presented in Barcelona reports that the oral medication daraxonrasib, combined with chemotherapy, caused tumour shrinkage in pancreatic cancer patients. In one in 12 patients, the cancer became undetectable. The treatment is being called the biggest breakthrough for the disease in decades.

stories.title: Radspherin safety data released in phase II trial
stories.summary: An interim safety analysis of an ongoing phase II trial for Radspherin reported no serious adverse events related to the treatment in patients with peritoneal metastases from ovarian cancer. These results represent the first randomized, controlled safety data for the drug. The trial remains ongoing.

stories.title: Daraxonrasib and chemotherapy combination shrinks metastatic pancreatic tumours
stories.summary: Results from a Phase I/II clinical trial indicate that daraxonrasib combined with chemotherapy leads to substantial tumour shrinkage in patients with metastatic pancreatic cancer. The findings suggest a potential new approach for treating cancer that has spread to other parts of the body.

stories.title: Cell biologists identify mechanism in childhood epilepsy
stories.summary: University of Liverpool scientists have mapped the positioning of a specific protein within nerve cells that is linked to a severe form of childhood epilepsy. The discovery provides new insights into the mechanics of this rare genetic neurological disorder.

stories.title: Inner ear research challenges hearing models
stories.summary: New research into how the inner ear processes sound challenges canonical understandings of human hearing. The findings could lead to future improvements in hearing technology, including cochlear implants. The ear has been found to be more complicated than previously assumed.

stories.title: Health Ministry marks World AMR Awareness Week
stories.summary: The Union Ministry of Health and Family Welfare has launched World Antimicrobial Resistance Awareness Week 2026. Officials warned that the misuse of antimicrobial medicines is undermining decades of medical progress, potentially making common infections difficult to treat. The ministry is requesting that people use antibiotics as intended.

stories.title: Delhi approves 10 lakh rupee health cover for transgender residents
stories.summary: The Delhi government has approved including transgender beneficiaries under the Ayushman Bharat health scheme. The coverage provides 10 lakh rupees annually, split between central and state funding. Beneficiaries will have access to over 1,900 treatment procedures across 27 medical specialties at empanelled hospitals.

stories.title: India reaches 10 million HPV vaccine milestone
stories.summary: India has administered over 10 million doses of the HPV vaccine in less than nine months. The campaign focuses on immunising young girls to reduce cervical cancer incidence. Health officials have described the initiative as a crucial step for women's health across the nation.

stories.title: India hits one crore HPV vaccinations in nine months
stories.summary: India has administered over 1 crore HPV vaccine doses to 14-year-old girls, covering 87 percent of its annual target. Six states, including Gujarat and Uttar Pradesh, have reached 100 percent of their identified target populations. The campaign aims to prevent cervical cancer through national immunisation.

stories.title: Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission reaches 939 million ABHA IDs
stories.summary: Union Health Minister J.P. Nadda announced that the Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission has reached over 939 million registered IDs. The government is now shifting focus toward maximising the adoption and utilisation of the digital health ecosystem. The mission is currently one of the world's largest.

stories.title: Thirteen dead following spurious liquor consumption in Manipur
stories.summary: At least 13 people have died and over 300 have been hospitalised in Manipur following the consumption of spurious liquor. Patients are receiving treatment across multiple facilities in Imphal for suspected methanol poisoning. The state government is currently monitoring the situation.

stories.title: Manipur reports 15 deaths from suspected spurious liquor
stories.summary: At least 15 people have died and 180 have been hospitalised in Manipur's Chandel district after consuming suspected spurious liquor. The deaths occurred between November 18 and 20. The district administration has issued a public health advisory and initiated preventive measures.

stories.title: India surpasses 80 lakh HPV vaccinations
stories.summary: The Union Ministry of Health and Family Welfare announced that India has crossed 80 lakh HPV vaccinations. The ministry described the milestone as an important step toward strengthening preventive healthcare and protecting against HPV-associated cancers. The nationwide campaign continues to target the prevention of cervical cancer.

stories.title: India reports 80 percent decline in malaria cases
stories.summary: The Union Health Ministry reports an 80 percent decline in malaria cases and deaths between 2015 and 2025. The number of high-burden districts dropped from 155 to 33, with 160 districts reporting zero indigenous cases. The ministry attributes the progress to targeted control and elimination measures.

stories.title: Israeli strike on vehicle in Gaza kills three, Gaza Health Ministry says - Reuters
Virginia reports first measles-associated child death of 2026
stories.summary: Virginia health officials confirmed a measles-associated death of a child aged four or younger. The state has recorded 220 cases this year, with 179 involving unvaccinated individuals. The death follows a national trend that recently cost the United States its measles elimination status after 26 years.

stories.title: South Korea records first cholera case in a decade
stories.summary: South Korean health authorities confirmed a cholera case in a patient who visited a hospital in Changwon. The individual had no recent history of overseas travel. Officials are currently tracing the source of the infection and contacts while urging the public to maintain safe water and food practices.

stories.title: Ebola vaccine trials to begin in DR Congo
stories.summary: The World Health Organisation announced that trials for two candidate vaccines targeting the Bundibugyo Ebola strain will begin in the Democratic Republic of Congo next week. The current outbreak has resulted in 5,568 deaths out of 11,376 confirmed cases, marking the country's worst-ever Ebola crisis.

stories.title: Virginia child death linked to worsening U.S. measles outbreak
stories.summary: A child between 0 and 4 years old has died in Virginia following a measles infection. State data shows 220 cases reported in 2026, with 179 occurring in unvaccinated individuals. The state health department did not disclose the child's vaccination status, citing family privacy.

stories.title: Yemeni Health Ministry reports 41 civilian deaths in airstrikes
stories.summary: The Yemeni Health Ministry stated that Saudi airstrikes killed 41 civilians, including 11 children and seven women, over a 24-hour period. These casualties bring the total death toll from the recent escalation to 438. The conflict has led to mutual blockades and ongoing military activity.

stories.title: Death toll from Kabul educational centre blast reaches 48
stories.summary: A suicide attack at an educational centre in the Dasht-e-Barchi area of Kabul has killed 48 people and wounded 67 others. The area is a Shia-majority neighbourhood. No group has claimed responsibility for the blast, which occurred after several weeks of relative calm in the capital.

stories.title: Health Ministry says 300 children died awaiting medical evacuation from Gaza
stories.summary: The Palestinian Health Ministry reported that 300 children have died while waiting for Israeli authorisation to leave Gaza for medical treatment. Another 5,400 children remain on evacuation lists. The ministry warned that current delays and restrictions are placing thousands of patients at immediate risk.

stories.title: Gaza health officials condemn detention of hospital director
stories.summary: The Gaza Health Ministry described the six-month detention extension of Kamal Adwan Hospital director Hussam Abu Safiya as a compound crime. The ministry stated the move is part of a systematic targeting of medical personnel and a violation of international norms protecting humanitarian workers.

stories.title: AIIMS expands voice-based prescription technology
stories.summary: AIIMS New Delhi and other medical services are rolling out the BHASHINI platform to support voice-based prescriptions and multilingual clinical documentation. The initiative, demonstrated at the Global Digital Health Summit 2026, aims to integrate artificial intelligence into hospital systems to facilitate communication across different Indian languages.

stories.title: Health secretary calls for linking cancer data to digital IDs
stories.summary: Union Health Secretary Punya Salila Srivastava stated that cancer screening records should be linked to Ayushman Bharat Health Account IDs. The ministry aims to use digital infrastructure to ensure continuity of care as patients transition between primary, secondary, and tertiary healthcare facilities.

stories.title: BHASHINI showcases multilingual AI at digital health summit
stories.summary: The Digital India BHASHINI Division presented its multilingual artificial intelligence ecosystem at the Global Digital Health Summit 2026. The division demonstrated how language technologies can streamline clinical workflows and promote patient-centric experiences. The platform is designed to enhance healthcare delivery through accessible and inclusive digital tools.

stories.title: BHASHINI highlights role of AI in inclusive healthcare
stories.summary: The Digital India BHASHINI Division concluded its participation at the Global Digital Health Summit 2026. The ministry showcased how multilingual artificial intelligence can strengthen healthcare delivery and facilitate clinical workflows. The platform aims to enable more accessible and patient-centric healthcare experiences through language technology.

stories.title: Google demonstrates AI healthcare tools in Visakhapatnam
stories.summary: Google officials presented AI-powered healthcare tools to district authorities in Visakhapatnam. The demonstration focused on potential applications for patient data management, diagnostic support, and resource planning across government health facilities. The company highlighted how these digital applications could assist in managing public health infrastructure.

stories.title: ICMR mental health platform wins e-governance award
stories.summary: The Indian Council of Medical Research received a Gold Award at the National Awards for e-Governance 2026 for its ICMR-MINDS platform. The initiative uses artificial intelligence to improve access to mental healthcare services. The award recognises the platform's contribution to citizen-centric service delivery.

stories.title: Jharkhand launches digital health initiatives
stories.summary: Jharkhand introduced several digital healthcare projects at the Digital Health Conclave 2026, including a Chief Minister Digital Health Scheme and a 10-bed Tele-ICU. The state also launched an HRIS portal and an e-Health portal as part of its effort to implement smarter healthcare infrastructure.

stories.title: ICMR reaches 100 medical technology transfers
stories.summary: The Indian Council of Medical Research has reached 100 technology transfers, according to the DHR-ICMR Health Research Excellence Summit. The milestone highlights the organisation's progress in translating indigenous health research into practical healthcare solutions for the Indian market.

stories.title: Healthcare leaders gather for digital summit in New Delhi
stories.summary: The Global Digital Health Summit 2026 in New Delhi brings together clinicians, policymakers, and technology experts to discuss the application of artificial intelligence in healthcare. The event focuses on exploring real-world uses for AI across the healthcare ecosystem.

stories.title: Workplace stress and anxiety
Welsh study to test mental health impact of under-16s social media ban
stories.summary: Researchers at Cardiff University and the University of Bristol will track the mental health of young people in Wales before and after a UK social media ban for under-16s. The study aims to determine if restrictions improve wellbeing. The government expects the ban to arrive soon.

stories.title: Study highlights need for community mental health support for refugees in India
stories.summary: A study of Sri Lankan Tamil and Rohingya populations in India finds mental health concerns are linked to legal uncertainty and social isolation. Published in the International Journal of Migration, Health and Social Care, it calls for training community members to recognise psychological needs in refugee populations.

stories.title: Shortage of clinical psychologists in Kerala government hospitals
stories.summary: Kerala has approximately 80,000 people with intellectual challenges but only 22 clinical psychologists across state government hospitals to conduct IQ assessments. The shortage leaves many waiting for necessary disability certificates. The state is currently operating with a limited pool of specialists for a large population.

stories.title: Study finds autistic adults show slower task adaptation during emotion
stories.summary: A trial of 120 autistic and 111 non-autistic adults using the Berlin Emotion Recognition Test revealed that autistic participants show reduced task adaptation over time. Researchers used automated facial analysis software to move beyond aggregate accuracy scores. The study suggests distinct patterns in how context moderates recognition.

stories.title: Study finds no mental health integration in Nigerian HIV and TB units
stories.summary: A baseline assessment in Niger State, Nigeria, found a complete absence of mental health service integration within high-volume HIV and tuberculosis treatment units. None of the surveyed facilities had incorporated mental health care into routine operations. Chronic infection management currently operates without these additional support services.

stories.title: Maternal mental health receives less than one percent of NIH research
stories.summary: Maternal mental health research received 0.06 percent of total NIH funding in fiscal year 2025, according to a report in Nature Mental Health. Despite perinatal conditions affecting one in five women, research investments remain at a fraction of a percent. The data covers the last decade.

stories.title: Study links postpartum mental health care gaps to structural barriers
stories.summary: A study of 13,000 women identifies economic and structural issues as primary barriers to postpartum mental health care. Researchers found that lack of childcare and difficulty finding information prevent access. The study suggests that logistical obstacles remain a significant factor in whether women receive necessary support.

stories.title: Young people in Colombia report climate anxiety
stories.summary: A study of people aged 18 to 28 in Colombia’s Aburrá Valley found that a majority experience sadness, fear, and guilt regarding environmental degradation. While 90 percent expressed a desire to take action, many reported feeling powerlessness about the future. The climate is currently affecting their outlook.

research.title: Microplastics may be more dangerous than we thought. Scientists just discovered why
research.summary: Microplastics may be doing something far more dangerous than simply accumulating in our bodies. Scientists have discovered that tiny plastic particles can interact with water to generate highly reactive molecules capable of damaging cells and tissues. This unexpected chemical activity could help explain growing evidence linking microplastic exposure.
